verses.text: Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them, "I am now a hundred and twenty years old, and I am no longer able to lead you. The LORD has told me, 'You will not cross the Jordan.'
The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations in front of you, and you will take over their land. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD said.
The LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, whom he destroyed along with their land.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you must do to them everything I have commanded you.
Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, for the LORD your God goes with you. He will never leave you or abandon you."

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him in front of all Israel, "Be strong and brave, for you must go with these people into the land the LORD promised their ancestors he would give them. You must divide it among them as their share.
The LORD himself goes ahead of you and will be with you. He will never leave you or abandon you. Do not be afraid, and do not lose heart."
So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the descendants of Levi, who carried the Ark of the LORD's Covenant, and to all the leaders of Israel.
Then Moses commanded them, "At the end of every seven years, in the year for cancelling debts, during the Festival of Shelters,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose, you must read this law aloud to all Israel so they can hear it.

Gather the people together, men, women, and children, and the foreigners living in your towns, so that they can listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and carefully obey all the words of this law.
Their children, who do not know this law, must also hear it and learn to fear the LORD your God for as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take over."
The LORD said to Moses, "The time of your death is near. Call Joshua and come to the Tent of Meeting, where I will give him his orders." So Moses and Joshua went and stood at the Tent of Meeting.
Then the LORD appeared at the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood over the entrance to the Tent.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are going to rest with your ancestors, and these people will soon be unfaithful to me. They will chase after the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me and break the covenant I made with them.

On that day my anger will burn against them. I will abandon them and hide my face from them, and they will be destroyed. Many disasters and troubles will come on them, and on that day they will ask, 'Have these disasters not come on us because our God is not with us?'
And I will certainly hide my face on that day because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods.
Now write down this song and teach it to the Israelites. Have them sing it, so that it may be a witness for me against them.

When I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey, the land I promised their ancestors, and when they have eaten all they want and become fat, they will turn to other gods and worship them. They will reject me and break my covenant.

And when many disasters and troubles come on them, this song will stand as a witness against them, because their descendants will not forget it. I know what they are planning even now, before I bring them into the land I promised them."
So Moses wrote down this song that same day and taught it to the Israelites.
The LORD gave this command to Joshua son of Nun: "Be strong and brave, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I promised them, and I myself will be with you."
Moses finished writing the words of this law in a book, from beginning to end.
Then he gave this command to the Levites who carried the Ark of the LORD's Covenant:
"Take this Book of the Law and put it beside the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD your God. It will stay there as a witness against you.
For I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still alive and with you, you have been rebelling against the LORD. How much more will you rebel after I die!
Gather to me all the leaders of your tribes and all your officials, so that I can speak these words to them and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after I die you are sure to become completely evil and turn away from the way I have commanded you. In days to come disaster will fall on you, because you will do what is evil in the LORD's sight and make him angry by what your hands have made."
Then Moses recited all the words of this song, from beginning to end, to the whole assembly of Israel.
